question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [City/Region — Geographical Location or Role in the Fall of Constantinople]
options: Constantinople — Located on the Bosphorus Strait, serving as the gateway between the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara
Galata (Pera) — A Genoese trading colony located across the Golden Horn from Constantinople
Adrianople (Edirne) — Captured by Ottomans in 1365 and made their capital before the fall of Constantinople
Bosphorus — The strait connecting the Aegean Sea directly to the Black Sea, controlled by Constantinople
wrong_fact: The Bosphorus does NOT connect the Aegean Sea directly to the Black Sea. It connects the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara; the Dardanelles (Hellespont) connects the Sea of Marmara to the Aegean Sea. The full passage from the Black Sea to the Aegean requires traversing both the Bosphorus and the Dardanelles.
explanation: The Bosphorus strait runs from the Black Sea in the north to the Sea of Marmara in the south — NOT to the Aegean Sea. The Dardanelles (further south/west) then connects the Sea of Marmara to the Aegean. Constantinople sat at the junction of the Bosphorus and the Sea of Marmara, making it the strategic gateway. The other options are correctly matched: Galata was a Genoese enclave on the northern shore of the Golden Horn; Adrianople (Edirne) was captured by Murad I in 1365 and served as the Ottoman capital before 1453.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Trade Route / City — Impact of the Fall of Constantinople (1453)]
options: Silk Road through Anatolia — Disrupted as Ottomans imposed heavy tolls on overland trade between Europe and Asia
Venice and Genoa — Italian city-states that lost their dominant trading privileges in the eastern Mediterranean and Black Sea
Alexandria (Egypt) — Remained a key hub for spice trade via the Red Sea–Mamluk route even after 1453
Trebizond (Trabzon) — A Byzantine successor state on the Caspian Sea coast that fell to Ottomans in 1461
wrong_fact: Trebizond (Trabzon) was NOT on the Caspian Sea coast — it is located on the southern coast of the Black Sea (in modern-day Turkey). It was the capital of the Empire of Trebizond, a Byzantine successor state, which fell to Mehmed II in 1461.
explanation: Trebizond (modern Trabzon) is situated on the Black Sea coast, not the Caspian Sea. It was the last surviving Byzantine successor state after the fall of Constantinople. Its fall in 1461 completed Ottoman control over the southern Black Sea coast. The other options are correctly matched: overland Silk Road trade was disrupted by Ottoman tolls; Venice and Genoa lost their trading colonies and privileges; Alexandria remained important as spices could still reach Europe via the Red Sea and Egypt under the Mamluks.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Ottoman Military / Geographical Strategy — Siege of Constantinople 1453]
options: Chain across the Golden Horn — Byzantines stretched a boom chain to block Ottoman ships from entering the harbour
Rumeli Hisarı (Boğazkesen) — Fortress built by Mehmed II in 1452 on the European side of the Bosphorus to cut off Byzantine supply lines from the Black Sea
Land walls of Theodosius — The triple-layered defensive walls on the western land side of Constantinople; breached during the final Ottoman assault
Anadolu Hisarı — Fortress built by Mehmed II on the European side of the Bosphorus opposite Rumeli Hisarı
wrong_fact: Anadolu Hisarı (meaning 'Anatolian Fortress') was built on the ASIAN (Anatolian) side of the Bosphorus, not the European side. It was constructed by Bayezid I around 1393–1394. Rumeli Hisarı, built by Mehmed II in 1452, is on the European side. Together they allowed the Ottomans to control the Bosphorus from both banks.
explanation: Anadolu Hisarı sits on the Asian (Anatolian) shore of the Bosphorus and was an older fortress built by Bayezid I. Mehmed II then built Rumeli Hisarı on the opposite European shore in 1452, creating a pincer that blockaded Constantinople from Black Sea supplies. The other options are correctly matched: the Byzantines did use a chain boom across the Golden Horn; the Theodosian Walls were the main land defences; Rumeli Hisarı was correctly built on the European side.
